> Im not entirely certain wether im dumb or not but ive tried to jam my airpods and it does not work, im not sure if airpods are a different spectrum or not? if anyone knows anything help would be appreciated!

Using narrow mode place nrf24 antenna between phone and airpods one by one 20-30cm. PHONE "30CM" > NRF24 ANTENNA "30CM" > AIRPODS you can also try on 2.4Ghz wi-fi network, just run it up and try get some website or ping google. Sience i've tested app in many scenarios i can assure you it works well. NRF is weak and without external PA you need place antenna close to reciever. Regards
I appreciate it, although now I’ve encountered a new problem, when I try to open the app it says it’s too new and does not work properly. It also is not detecting my nrf24. Any suggestions?

I also would like to say that I built this app using ufbt, moved it to my flipper running the latest version of momentum, and while the app runs (with a version warning about it potentially being incompatible) it fails to jam anything, even when it’s a hair’s breadth from the tx/rx

I don't support Momentum and I do not intend to in the future until they fix their hodgepodge, use Unleashed. Keep in mind that the amount of background bloat your firmware runs impacts its ability to properly drive the external chips.

title: [SUGGESTION LIST] - Various improvements/bug fixes
body:
Hi @huuck, 

As discussed in #2, here's a list of suggestions to implement/improve/fix!

I'm unfortunately not experienced with Flipper development so I won't be of much use on that front, but you can let met know if you need someone for testing, or further ideas! I'll keep this issue updated as needed. Or I can open new ones if you prefer.

### Bug fixes:
- The app randomly freezes. Sometimes this occurs shortly after opening it, sometimes during jamming, and sometimes not at all. The Flipper does not explicitly crash, but it becomes completely frozen and requires a hard reboot (with ```<``` + ```Back```) 

### Improvements / further implementations:
- The app could benefit from a "Status" indicator, letting the user know what state it is in. (idle, jamming...)
- Add the ability to target specific hopping frequencies, either by presets and/or custom values, or generally more automatic patterns
- Similarly, we could add a feature to allow fine tuning the frequency to a given channel (2400-2483.5 MHz range for Bluetooth/Wi-Fi with 1 MHz of channel bandwidth or 2 MHz ch. bandwidth for BLE)
- We could maybe specify a target type (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, BLE or more generic) of jamming, and have presets tuned for these targets more specifically
- Ability to tune the TX power of the NRF24 module at runtime, if that's possible
author: Kyhze

comments.body:
- I'm investigating the freeze, must be some kind of stupid race condition that causes it. 
- Status indicator - not planned but it's an easy win. Maybe even blink the LED or something.
- Custom channels is also in the work, current flow is to load a file of channels separated by commas. Problem is the Flipper does not render the file selection dialog for some reason :/ I'll keep poking at it
- Channel bandwidth selection does not make any sense from what I could see, there's no reason in using anything other than 2MHz bandwidth (the nRF fills the 2MHz channel as fast as the 1MHz one), so I don't plan on supporting this as it will only cause problems when people will complain that "the app does not work" when put in 1MHz mode.
- I do not endorse any targeted attacks against WiFi/BT, this is just a toy and should be treated as one :)
- PA TX power is set to max by default (if the chip supports it), otherwise it doesn't really do anything, not planning on changing this as it will just introduce another parameter that people will play with and possibly make the signal too weak.
good suggestions, +1 for that freezing bug fix, might i suggest a dolphin on the screen that turns crazy  when you run it?

Update: Blinking the LED is not an option (or any animation). I need all of Flipper's resources to drive the nRF (the fact that I can't continuously push it seems to be the main reason why it fares worse than driving it directly from an ESP). So we'll ahve to stick with the text it displays.
Custom channels are IN! Check the readme.
Other than that, there's no reason to add bandwidth/PA TX power selectors since this is already maxed out (tested all the combination and it fares worse). If you have additional ideas, feel free to submit a PR!. Closing this for now, for additional feature requests feel free to open a new ticket.
